sources.entry: A blog is a discussion or informational website consisting of discrete, diary-style text entries (posts).

summary.name: Blog (Wikipedia article)
summary.one_liner: Wikipedia article explaining what a blog is, its history from the late 1990s onward, the types of blogs, and the software used to build them.
use_cases: comparing blog platforms and self-hosting options
summary.what_it_does: The article defines a blog as a website whose basic unit is a dated post, usually shown in reverse chronological order. It traces blogging from early terms like "weblog" (1997) and "blog" (1999) through early hosted tools such as Open Diary, LiveJournal, and Blogger. It describes blog categories including personal, collaborative, microblog, corporate, aggregated, and media-type blogs such as vlogs and photoblogs. It also summarizes blog software options, including managed platforms like Medium and Substack and self-hosted tools like WordPress, Hugo, and Jekyll.
notable: Covers the history of blogging from 1990s online diaries to the 2000s political influence of blogs
Lists blog types by genre, media format, and device
Names software options from managed platforms to self-hosted static site generators
caveats: Article is marked as needing an update (July 2026)
Some statistics and claims are dated (for example, 2006 and 2008 rankings)
